Name: Sojourner Truth
Summary: African American abolitionist and itinerant preacher, born enslaved in New York, who renamed herself Sojourner Truth in 1843 and travelled preaching abolition and women's rights, famously asking 'Ain't I a woman?'
Contribution: Preached abolition and women's rights from her own experience of slavery, becoming a symbol of faith-fuelled freedom speaking.
Testimony: She testified that God called her to travel and declare truth, and that her freedom was God's gift to proclaim.
